questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to to go a country where the nature is very different from the danish. Before I went to Iceland, I haven't been to another Scandinavian country. And I think that it feels weird not to visit your neighbors before you go to a country on the other side of the earth. And we have so much shared history in common. I think that is important to know about. So i chose to go to Reykjavik. Beautiful nature and so much art and culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We got an e-mail from a mentor, that we always could text if we needed help with anything.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was unfortunately not that easy and its often really expensive in Iceland. I have some Icelandic family and they texted all they new in Iceland and asked them if they had a cheap room i could rent. But I have two danish friends that wrote a post in a Facebook-group for Danish people in Iceland. And they got a lot of help in that group. So a recommendation could be to look at Facebook-groups for Danish people who lives in the country you are going to.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I think you learn more about the culture in the country by living off campus. I lived with an Icelandic man and he told me a lot about Iceland that i would not have know if I lived in studenthousing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was easy. I went to an information desk in the main building and they registered my arrival.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could ask them about anything - also how to get discount on bus cards

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: That was a bit more difficult. I remember that many of my classes overlapped by time, and it was hard to see which other available courses that could match my schedule because it was not showed on the web side. But I just went to the information desk and asked them about it.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take it chill. It will work out. And do not be afraid to ask to many questions. If you are in doubt about something,  just go to the information desk.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I think that it is overwhelming to have 4 courses in one semester. It just get more superficial and you never really dive deep in to the material. Furthermore it seems like some of the courses have way too many expectations and reading material for an 5-ects course. Other courses are very easy and it feels weird that it is on a University level. 
But I also had courses that I was really happy about and found very interesting.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Being Icelandic: Too many expectations for the student in a 5-ects course. Way to much reading material, tests, assignments and an interview for a 5-ects course. But it was not the content that was difficult, there were just to many things we needed to do.

Nordic Movies and Television: Our teacher did not really teach us anything. It seemed a bit like he did not know anything about the content of the course. 

Danish contemporary literature: I was really happy about this course. I learned a lot and the teacher was really good.

Cognitive linguistics and literature: It was an okay course. But I had expected that it would involve more reading of literature.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teachers are much better in Copenhagen

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: I did that above

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Danish contemporary literature: If you are interested in contemporary danish literature, I would recommend this course. I learned a lot and there were so much time for discussions and close reading.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Iceland is really expensive i general. It is hard to come out and see the country without a car. So I spend more money on renting cars that I had expected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Alcohol and going out to eat is really expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Gym, meditation class, the University offered whale safari trips, parties and a lot more

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go on some of the arranged trips. It is cheaper and it is a nice way to get in touch with the other students

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Get out in the nature. Iceland is so beautiful. Rent a summerhouse in the nature with some of you new friends.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy for med because I lived with an Icelander. But in general I think it was easy to talk with Icelanders in the night-life in Reykjavik.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I don't know. Be open and not too pushy

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I found it challenging that Icelanders are really relaxed about practical stuff and bad at time schedules. Some are also really closed and introvert and you need to ask a lot to get the information you need.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Maybe also the thing that I found challenging. Everything is just a bit more chill in Iceland. And I think you can learn a lot from that as a Danish person.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Everything will work out. 
Have a saving before you go. It is a really expensive country to live in.
Get out of the city in the weekends and experience the beautiful nature

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not be afraid of asking to much if you are in doubt about something.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To meet so many sweet people. And experience incredible nature. I felt so relaxed and happy in the nature.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To learn to be more alone and feel good about it. It took some time.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
